subject.title: fix: provider usage accounting, retry/overflow classification, and output clamping

question: Should omitting `maxRetries` from the public Anthropic stream API preserve the SDK's existing default, or should OpenClaw redefine omission to mean zero retries?
rationale: Both behaviors are technically possible, but choosing between public-call compatibility and centralized outer-retry policy changes existing caller semantics and requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Preserve omission semantics
options.body: Leave the provider API's unset value untouched and pass zero explicitly only from OpenClaw call sites that already own an outer retry loop.

options.title: Redefine the provider default
options.body: Keep unconditional zero retries, but treat it as an intentional compatibility change with direct-caller tests and upgrade documentation.

recommendation.title: Preserve omission semantics
recommendation.body: Leave the provider API's unset value untouched and pass zero explicitly only from OpenClaw call sites that already own an outer retry loop.

likelyOwner.reason: The LLM package-boundary history and current provider work make this the strongest available owner for the public retry-contract choice.
